LOOK.text: Below, in smaller print: 'Accepting patients 24/7. No appointment needed. Your wallet is your referral.'

USE.text: I tap the sign. It doesn't take bookings. It barely takes rain.

TALK.text: 'Hello?' The sign keeps its own counsel. Very clinical.

PICK.text: I tug the sign. Institutional-grade screws. This clinic takes signage seriously.

OPEN.text: Signs don't open. This one just stares until you admit things.

CLOSE.text: 'Always open,' says the sign. Says the sign next to a locked door.

PUSH.text: I push the sign. It doesn't budge. Neither does my opinion of it.

PULL.text: I pull the sign. A screw loosens. I tighten it back. I'm a guest. Sort of.

GIVE.text: The sign doesn't want anything. The drop box, on the other hand, is hungry.

PULL.text: I pull the handle. The scanner beeps. It's the angry beep.

PICK.text: I'm not taking the door. They'd notice. It's the only door.

CLOSE.text: It's already shut. Extremely shut. Shut with intent.

GIVE.text: Doors don't take gifts. The visitor box takes evidence. Different department.

The box hums and returns it. Apparently that's not a medical condition.
Scanned and returned. Rejected. Even the box has standards.
sign_in_sheet: I put the sheet back in the drop box. Then take it out again. Evidence first, manners later.

hotspots.name: Visitor Drop Box

LOOK.text: A weathered drop box labeled 'VISITOR SIGN-IN'. A newer slot underneath: 'PROOF OF SYMPTOMS. SCANNED AND RETURNED.'

else.text: There's a clipboard inside.
A sign-in sheet with a barcode at the bottom. Names on the list: 'V. Buterin (discharged)', 'S. Bankman (transferred)', 'D. Kwon (escaped)'.
At the very bottom: 'Patient Zero — [REDACTED]'. The barcode might work on the scanner.

OPEN.text: I open the drop box lid. The sign-in sheet is right there.

USE.text: The slot wants evidence, not my hand. Proof of symptoms. I have plenty. I need it in a form.

TALK.text: I whisper 'Hello?' into the slot. It echoes. Just me and some clipboards. My usual crowd.

CLOSE.text: I close the lid. Click. Very final. Like a nurse saying 'next.'

PUSH.text: I push the drop box. Bolted down. Somebody here has had things stolen before.

PULL.text: I pull the drop box. It stays. Nobody's running off with the visitor logs. Not today.

GIVE.text: The slot takes proof of symptoms. It scans them and gives them back. Like a pawn shop for feelings.

LOOK.text: Brutalist concrete. The kind of building where hope goes for a reality check.
No windows on the ground floor. Privacy for the patients. Or for the staff.

TALK.text: I say hello. The concrete eats it. Lovely acoustics, for screaming.

USE.text: Use the whole building? I'll start with the door. Baby steps.

PICK.text: I can't pick up a building. I checked my pockets. They agreed.

OPEN.text: You don't open a building. You open its door. I'm told that's the trick.

CLOSE.text: I can't close a building. That's a job for the council and a lot of paperwork.

PUSH.text: I push against the concrete wall. It doesn't move. Built different. Literally.

PULL.text: I pull the building toward me. Civil engineering wins. It usually does.

GIVE.text: The building only accepts patients. It's very clear about that. In concrete.

glasses_3d: I show the camera my spare 3D glasses. It doesn't recognise me. Nobody does in these.

LOOK.text: A camera tracks my movement. Red LED blinks steadily. Someone is watching.
Or something. Nobody blinks that steadily. Except cameras. And Penny.

TALK.text: 'Nice lens.' The camera doesn't take compliments. It takes footage.

USE.text: I wave at the camera. The LED blinks faster. We're basically friends now.

PICK.text: I reach for the camera. The LED panics. I think I just triggered an alert. Smooth.

OPEN.text: I'm not prying open the camera. It's recording me deciding not to. Good choice, Dex.

CLOSE.text: I cover the lens. The camera turns away from my hand. Camera-shy. In a camera.

PUSH.text: I nudge the camera up. Now it films the sky. I nudge it back. I'm not a vandal. Yet.

PULL.text: I pull the camera. The bracket groans. So does someone behind the intercom.

GIVE.text: The camera already has my face. From every angle. Including the bad one.

LOOK.text: A bench for visitors. Carved into the armrest: 'WAGMI' crossed out, replaced with 'NGMI', crossed out, replaced with '???'.

USE.text: I sit for a moment. The mountain air is cold. The bench is personally colder.
Someone scratched initials into the seat. Too worn to read. Waiting rooms do that to people.

TALK.text: I tell the bench my problems. It's heard worse. It's heard them from this exact spot.

PICK.text: I try to lift the bench. Cemented down. Even the furniture here was admitted for life.

OPEN.text: I check under the bench seat. Gum, a lost coin, and a tiny note: 'DYOR before sitting.'

CLOSE.text: Benches don't close. They just wait. Like everyone else out here.

PUSH.text: I push the bench. It doesn't move. It's made its peace with this spot.

PULL.text: I pull on the armrest. The carved 'WAGMI' catches my finger. Even graffiti has sharp edges.

GIVE.text: The bench has received enough. Mostly butts and bad news.

LOOK.text: "SERENITY PRAYER: Grant me serenity to accept trades I cannot reverse, courage to HODL the ones I can, and wisdom to know the difference."
"12 STEPS TO RECOVERY: Step 1 — Disconnect your wallet. Steps 2-12 — See Step 1."

USE.text: The posters are laminated. Somebody here really believes in these posters.

TALK.text: I read the serenity prayer aloud. For a moment, I actually feel serene. Then I remember my open leveraged positions.

PICK.text: I try to peel a poster off. Laminated AND glued. Motivation, permanently installed.

OPEN.text: I lift a corner. Behind it, an older poster: 'HANG IN THERE.' A kitten. Also hanging in there.

CLOSE.text: I smooth the poster flat. The 12 Steps stare back. All twelve of them, judging.

PUSH.text: I push on the poster. Solid wall behind. No secret passage. I always check.

PULL.text: I pull at the edge. It peels slightly, revealing handwritten text: 'Step 13: Buy the dip anyway.' Someone relapsed.

GIVE.text: The posters are free. The catch is admitting they're about you.

receipt: I'm not throwing the receipt away. It's the saddest thing I own. I keep it for perspective.

hotspots.name: Trash Can

LOOK.text: A metal trash can. Overflowing with crumpled papers, empty energy drink cans, and what appears to be a torn-up whitepaper titled 'SafeMoon v3.'

USE.text: I dig through the trash. Wet paper, cans, a banana with a past. Detective work is glamorous.

TALK.text: I peer into the bin. It stares back. Both of us full of other people's bad decisions.

then.text: Nothing else in there. Just regret and a banana peel.

else.text: And an empty can of BULL RUN. Somebody else couldn't sleep either. I'll take it. For science.

then.text: And an empty can of BULL RUN. Somebody else couldn't sleep either. I'll take it. For science.
I lift the lid. Empty cans. A banana peel. Somebody's resolve.

else.text: I lift the lid. The smell hits first. Then I spot something crumpled at the bottom...

CLOSE.text: I close the lid. Gently. The smell was getting ideas.

PUSH.text: I push the bin. It scrapes on the concrete. Somewhere inside, the nurse winces.

PULL.text: I pull the bin closer. Every good detective checks the bins. I read that on a bin.

GIVE.text: The bin takes everything, no questions asked. The only thing here without paperwork.

LOOK.text: 'Gwei' and 'Degen', spray-painted. Nurse Gwei must love that.

USE.text: I trace the letters. Still tacky. Whoever did this was recent. And not yet cured.

TALK.text: I read it aloud: 'Gwei.' The intercom crackles, offended. I didn't write it, Nurse.

PICK.text: I can't peel paint off concrete. I tried with a nail. Now my nail is 'Degen' too.

OPEN.text: Nothing to open. Graffiti is all front, no back.

CLOSE.text: I can't close graffiti. I could stand in front of it. That's not a long-term plan.

PUSH.text: I push the tagged wall. The paint doesn't smudge. Good paint. Bad decisions.

PULL.text: I scratch at the graffiti. Under 'Gwei' someone wrote 'was here' in pencil. Under THAT: 'we are all here.'

GIVE.text: The graffiti was a gift to the world. The world didn't ask. It rarely does.

LOOK.text: A cracked walkway to the entrance. Weeds push through. Even the weeds want in.

USE.text: I follow the path. Step on a crack... no. I've had enough bad luck this month.

TALK.text: I hum on the path. The echo hums back, slightly off-key. Probably me.

PICK.text: I pick up a pebble. I put it back. It was here first.

OPEN.text: The path is open. Paths usually are. That's their whole thing.

CLOSE.text: I can't close a path. That's the council's job. They don't do mountains.

PUSH.text: I push on. Each step closer to Patient Zero. My calves would like a word.

PULL.text: This place pulls me in and pushes me back at the same time. Like a dentist.

GIVE.text: The path already gives directions. To the door. It's got one idea.

intro.speaker: Nurse Gwei
intro.text: Evidence received. Insomnia: confirmed. Loss: confirmed. Now, denial. Do you have a problem?

choices.text: Problem? I've never even heard of crypto.
I can stop whenever I want. I just don't want to.

liar.text: That's lying, not denial. Denial is when you believe it.

bye.text: The intercom is always on. Unlike your stop-losses.
